definitions.explanation: The way a person carries themselves in speech and behavior, especially as perceived by others. Often used to describe an overall impression of someone's social deportment.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{物腰|ものごし}が{柔|やわ}らかい。
{物腰|ものごし}の{丁寧|ていねい}な{人|ひと}だという{印象|いんしょう}を{受|う}けた。
examples.english: I got the impression that he was a person with polite manners.

examples.japanese: {穏|おだ}やかな{物腰|ものごし}の{裏|うら}に{強|つよ}い{意志|いし}を{感|かん}じた。
examples.english: I sensed a strong will behind the calm demeanor.

notes:
USAGE:
{物腰|ものごし} refers to the overall impression someone gives through their behavior, posture, and speech. It is almost always modified by an adjective: {物腰|ものごし}が{柔|やわ}らかい (gentle manner), {物腰|ものごし}が{丁寧|ていねい} (polite bearing).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {物腰|ものごし}が{柔|やわ}らかい (gentle in manner)
- {物腰|ものごし}が{丁寧|ていねい} (polite in bearing)
- {穏|おだ}やかな{物腰|ものごし} (calm demeanor)
- {上品|じょうひん}な{物腰|ものごし} (refined bearing)
- {物腰|ものごし}の{低|ひく}い{人|ひと} (a humble, unassuming person)
